To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The radiolarian assemblage distributions in the equatorial and subtropical Pacific Ocean reflect major features of the equatorial oceanographic circulation system, such as western tropical mixed layer flows, eastern upwelling, the oxygen minimum layer, and subtropical gyres.

the distributions of radiolarian faunal assemblages in the surface sediments of the equatorial Pacific Ocean reflect the major surface and sub-surface characteristics of the oceanic circulation system and that fluctuations in the distributions of radiolarians during the last 125 000 yr reflect fluctuations in the position and intensity of the tradewinders.
the distribution of radiolarians in the surface waters of the eastern equator has been used to infer the history of equatorial Pacific atmospheric circulation during the last 120 000 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a quantitative methodology for the analysis of planktonic microfossil assemblages and the application of this methodology to the study of paleoceanographic changes during the last 125 000 years in the equatorial eastern Pacific.
reconstructing the history of the equatorial Pacific Ocean and the atmosphere during the last 130 000 yr.
the reconstruction of paleoenvironmental conditions during the last glacial cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the equatorial Pacific Ocean is a sensitive indicator of changes in the global climate system.
the distribution of equatorial Pacific radiolarians reflects changes in the tradewind circulation system.
the distribution of radiolarians in surface sediments is controlled primarily by the tradewind circulation system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
changes in the position of tradewind maxims in the eastern Pacific during the last 125 000 years have been related to fluctuations in ice volume and to the intensity of oceanic circulation.
the glacial-intergalcial cycle is not a cycle in the sense of a periodic oscillation of a system, but rather an irregular series of fluctuations.
during stage 4, the tradewinds were weaker and more zonal than during stage 2, and during the last 20 000 yr, the tradewind belt has migrated northward and intensified.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of planktonic foraminifer and radiolarian species in equatorial Pacific sediments is a sensitive indicator of the position and strength (and perhaps zonality) of the tradewinders.

changes in the distribution of surface water masses in the eastern equatorial Pacific are a sensitive indicator of changes in the tradewind circulation and can be used to infer past changes in tradewind circulation.
the distribution of radiolarians in surface sediments is controlled by the position and strength and tradewind systems, and by the position of the equatorial divergence zone.
